content.text:
You are a TLA+ specification engineer. You will receive a natural language description of a system. Produce a complete, syntactically correct TLA+ specification that faithfully captures the described behavior. The output must be a valid TLA+ module that passes the SANY parser. Include the MODULE declaration, EXTENDS, CONSTANTS, VARIABLES, Init, Next and Spec. Include all safety invariants and liveness properties described, and any fairness conditions mentioned. Output only the TLA+ specification.

System description: The module specifies an abstract model of the termination detection problem in a ring of N nodes with asynchronous message passing. Each node has an activation status (`active`) and a count of messages pending delivery (`pending`), and a boolean `terminationDetected` records whether termination has been globally observed. The system is considered truly terminated when every node is inactive and no messages are in flight.

In the initial state, nodes may be active or inactive with no pending messages, and termination may already be flagged if all nodes happen to be inactive. The four actions are: `Terminate`, where an active node deactivates and may optionally set `terminationDetected` if the system is already terminated; `SendMsg`, where an active node increments the pending count at any destination node; `RcvMsg`, where a node with pending messages consumes one and becomes active; and `DetectTermination`, which sets `terminationDetected` to true whenever the system is truly terminated. The overall specification `Spec` is the initial condition, the always-enabled next-state relation, and weak fairness on `DetectTermination`, ensuring termination is eventually detected once it occurs.

The safety property `Safe` asserts that `terminationDetected` implies actual termination. The liveness property `Live` asserts that true termination eventually leads to detection. `Quiescence` asserts that once terminated the system remains terminated. An inductive invariant `IndInv` combining `TypeOK` and `Safe` is provided for Apalache verification, along with action-formula variants of quiescence. The model is checked with N=4 and a state constraint bounding pending counts to at most 3.
